source_categories.retained_code_revision: A non-documentation source revision remains relative to D. This includes partial or invalid revisions and does not imply a correct repair.
source_categories.removed_requested_draft_logic: The returned source removes logic explicitly requested in the public issue that was present in D.
source_categories.quote_syntax_repair: Escaped source quoting is repaired, while other syntax defects remain observable.
source_categories.docstring_only: The business source difference from D consists only of a docstring addition.
source_categories.temporary_edit_restored: Business source was changed during the branch but restored to D before delivery.

checks.rationale: The issue requires too_early=425; three repository attribute/dictionary assertions complete. Existing aliases and other status names are outside the check.
The six real Prompt.check_choice assertions cover default sensitivity and ASCII insensitive matches. Prompt.ask interaction, whitespace, and Unicode are untested.
UploadFile's real schema has the requested contentMediaType replacement. Whole-dictionary equality is stronger than the issue's field requirement and cannot certify raw bytes or all routes.
The string alias direction is supported, but an inline decorator causes SyntaxError before any request.
Three schema-name presence checks do not specify input/output separation. The single-line class definition causes SyntaxError before OpenAPI generation.
Single-leading-slash path_url expectations follow the public issue, but the inline class statement prevents all assertions.
Empty Optional[int] form values should use None, but the inline decorator is a checking-program syntax failure.
Both requested lower/upper-case aliases equal 425 after importing the workspace Requests source. Old aliases are not checked.
The public Form-model multi-value reproduction reaches TestClient and completes the 200/list assertions. Single-value and other parameter types are outside scope.

The independent target node receives 422 for an empty Optional[int] form field, contradicting the required 200/None behavior. Two unrelated async collection failures do not erase this target failure; the JSON assertion is not reached.
Hashability is required, but equality and set deduplication of separately constructed instances are additional assumptions. The missing here-document prevents Python execution.
The issue concerns typed return annotations and bodiless routes; a generic helper identity assertion expands that contract. Python treats PY as a missing file, so no helper call runs.
Console.print(None, end='!') prints None! and continues to Done. The public title does not establish None as an empty call or no-crash as the full requirement.
The Response/Depends annotation is supported, but app construction fails on on_startup before the dependency endpoint is registered.
The requested tilde URL reaches ReprHighlighter. The single span starts at zero but ends before the full URL; failure occurs at the endpoint assertion, not span count or style.
Three self-contained partial dependencies resolve via a real request and return foo. Async callable instances and generator combinations are not covered.
The real parser excludes the parameter lacking '=', while preserving charset=utf-8. The assertion does not cover all Content-Type grammar.
Two real requests exercise a cache/reawaitable wrapped async dependency and obtain bar. The simplified Settings class and modified cached generator do not validate every wrapper or generator case.
The real codes object lacks the explicitly requested too_early attribute. This fails before the upper-case alias assertion.
The real fast-path predicate matches four ordinary single-width examples. Public source supports the limited predicate interpretation; full Unicode range and performance claims do not follow.
The OpenAPI response includes /root in servers, contradicting the visible requirement. The first failure prevents the Swagger escaping check from running.

The real Prompt.ask path accepts insensitive input and rejects it under explicit/default sensitivity. Return-case expectations are consistent with the visible process_response implementation, not a new issue-wide contract.
The public three-route/two-model reproduction generates anyOf length two. Reference identity and all route entries are not independently asserted.

Empty-path inclusion completes. GET '/' fails the inferred 200 requirement, but the public title only explicitly requires allowing the empty route; this does not provide a strict grounded contradiction.

The issue requires request-uri normalization, not necessarily rewriting PreparedRequest.url. The missing here-document fails first; the intended Request call also misplaces the URL in the method argument.
The explicit ESC0..ESC? range is supported. Python is invoked on a nonexistent PY file, so the tokenizer and preservation checks never run.
The Query model alias and extra-name checks correspond to the two public defects. Missing shell-to-Python wrapping prevents both tests; Header/Cookie are untested.
The FastAPI object lacks the explicitly requested frontend API. File-serving and router assertions are later and unexecuted; the observed API failure alone establishes the contradiction.
All three explicitly requested parser API-name assertions complete. hasattr neither verifies a property value nor executes reset, keep-alive, request reading, or shutdown.
The real parser excludes a malformed parameter with no '=' and retains the valid charset. The returned content type and other grammar cases are not asserted.
One real request awaits the issue's cache/reawaitable dependency and returns bar. Repeat awaiting and generator classification remain outside this check.
The explicitly requested alias resolves to 425 via real attribute and dictionary access. Upper-case and old aliases are untested.
The real single-width fast-path predicate matches p and ~. This neither validates every character in the extended range nor measures performance.
The requested pickle roundtrip completes and preserves JSONDecodeError type. The check does not assert msg/doc/pos values or execute a process pool.
Table(highlight=True).add_row creates columns that fail the directly requested highlight inheritance assertion. Other table/highlighter settings are outside scope.

The missing-key request passes the 401 status assertion but fails the visible ApiKey query header-format requirement. The issue warns that parts are outdated; the later 403 compatibility scenario is not executed.
The real scalar int=Form(None) route returns 200 and q=None for q=''. This does not certify models, aliases, file fields, or all regressions.

The model Header path accepts an underscored name under the default conversion setting, directly contradicting the issue. Four scalar assertions and the model hyphen case pass first; the final model-disabled scenarios are not reached.
The callback-execution direction is public, but the shell wrapping fails before app construction. The app.lifespan trigger itself is not independently validated.
Route inclusion is public; resolving the empty string to a 200 root request is an additional assumption. Missing here-document wrapping prevents either stage.

Importing an internal compatibility module emits the expected message substring. The issue concerns using pydantic.v1; exact wording, warning category, user trigger, and silence without v1 use are not established.

The reader-preservation direction matches the public source, but this class directly defines read instead of proxying it. An unterminated f-string prevents parsing, so no protocol fallback is exercised.
